# Sampling and Integration Schemes


## Overview
Sampling and Integration Schemes define the computational framework for sampling volumetric data along camera rays and aggregating those samples into final pixel colors . This family encompasses methods that determine where to sample the volume (stochastic vs. deterministic spacing) and how to aggregate those samples (compositing, projection, or approximation) [G]. It is distinguished from [Interpolation and Sampling Techniques](2787-interpolation-and-sampling-techniques.md) by focusing on the integration logic and sampling distribution rather than the spatial interpolation kernel [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Interpolation and Sampling Techniques](2787-interpolation-and-sampling-techniques.md), which covers the query positioning, kernel/weight application, and coordinate transformation common to all children [G].

## Subtopics

### [Monte Carlo Volume Rendering](2060-monte-carlo-volume-rendering.md)
A stochastic approach that replaces uniform spatial sampling with probabilistic distance sampling and null-collision scattering events. It is chosen when simulating complex light transport phenomena like multiple scattering in heterogeneous media, where deterministic methods are computationally prohibitive.

### [Ray Traversal and Integration Schemes](8341-ray-traversal-and-integration-schemes.md)
Defines the reduction logic that maps a sequence of discretized ray samples to a final pixel output via deterministic, grid-aligned traversal. It is chosen for standard direct volume ray casting where order-dependent integration (e.g., front-to-back compositing) is required.

### [Pre-integration and Approximation Methods](12352-pre-integration-and-approximation-methods.md)
Accelerates rendering by replacing on-the-fly evaluation of non-linear transfer functions with pre-computed lookup tables. It is chosen to eliminate aliasing artifacts caused by low sampling frequencies and to decouple transfer function frequency from sampling rate.

### [Order-Dependent Sampling Strategies](16277-order-dependent-sampling-strategies.md)
Resolves the order-dependence of sampling operations required for numerical solutions of integrals in volumetric lighting. It is chosen when illumination calculations depend on the specific sequence of samples relative to light sources, using iterative processing or precomputation.

## Background
The family originates from the fundamental volume rendering equation formulated by Williams et al. . Early implementations relied on uniform sampling and front-to-back compositing [G]. Monte Carlo methods were adapted from photon mapping techniques to handle participating media . Pre-integration was introduced to address the "missing peak" problem in transfer functions .

## Sources

[S2] Krivine, J. (2012). GPU-based Monte Carlo Volume Rendering.
